summary: sync's {"event":"sync_summary",...} line names its warned-resource count resources_warned, not warned. A regen must keep this name and keep the count meaning "resources whose run ended in a warning state" (e.g. access-denied skips) rather than a raw tally of sync_warning lines -- a single resource can emit multiple sync_warning events (pagination cap hits, non-incremental notices, cursor issues) while still completing successfully and being counted under success instead.
reason: Live testing found the plain warned field undercounted relative to the number of sync_warning lines actually seen in a run's event stream, since it only tallies resources whose terminal result carried a Warn, not every sync_warning event emitted along the way. Correctly counting total warning events would require instrumenting every sync_warning emission site across the flat/dependent pagination loops (several of which run concurrently), which is disproportionate for a low-priority cosmetic mismatch -- renaming to resources_warned and documenting the distinction in sync's own --help text resolves the ambiguity without that risk.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green; existing sync tests (channel_workflow_test.go, sync_hint_test.go) only assert on the sync_summary event name, not the field name, so no test changes were needed.
